Question_text: Fig. 1.1(a) shows a flower very shortly after it has opened and Fig. 1.1(b) shows the same flower when it is several days older. (a) On Fig. 1.1(b), label a filament and a sepal. (b) State two features of the flower in Fig. 1.1(a) that could have attracted the insect. (c) (i) explain why flowers of this plant are rarely self-pollinated (ii) suggest how the insect brings about pollination in this species of plant.
Unit: UNIT 16: Development of organisms and continuity of life

Question_text: Fig. 2.1 shows components of the faeces of a cow, an herbivorous mammal. (a) Name the component that makes up 75% of the faeces. (b) Suggest what makes up a major part of the fibre in the faeces. (c) Identify the component in faeces that is responsible for this increase in nitrates and describe its conversion into nitrates.(d) Explain why a mixture of faeces and urine is a better fertiliser than faeces alone.

Fig. 3.1 shows the human digestive system. (a) Identify parts C and D on Fig. 3.1. (b) (i) Use a label line on Fig. 3.1, marked ‘X', to indicate where fat digestion begins. (ii) Explain your reasons for selecting this region.(c) Adrenaline reduces the secretion of mucus in the body. Suggest why a person who suffers from stress may also suffer from damage to the lining of their stomach wall.

Fig. 4.1 shows the blood groups of the members of two families. (a) State the term used to describe the relationship between alleles IA and IB. (b) Identify, by number, which one of the children had been adopted by their family and could not be the genetic offspring of the parents. Explain your answer. (c) When children 4 and 5 grow up, they have a child of their own, child 8, as shown in Fig. 4.1. Using a genetic diagram, explain the possible genotypes and phenotypes of child 8.

Fig. 5.1 shows the rate of water uptake and of water loss for a plant over a 24-hour period. (a) Determine the rate of water uptake at 1200 hours.(b) (i) Name the cells through which water is absorbed from the soil.(ii) Name the cells between which water vapour passes to the atmosphere.(c) (i) State three uses of water within a plant between midnight and 0400 hours.(ii) State two additional uses of water between 0800 and 1900 hours.(d) Explain what may happen to the plant between 1400 and 1800 hours.
Topic: 7.1 Uptake and transport of water and ions
